subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equation of the radical axis of the circles x² + y² − 3x − 4y + 5 = 0, 3(x² + y²) − 7x + 8y − 11 = 0.

mark_split.label: Write both circles in standard form
Subtract to find the radical axis

insider_note: Only the second circle needs dividing by its leading coefficient here — the first circle is already standard, so do not scale it by mistake while standardising the second.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write both circles in standard form
steps.margin_note: First mark. The first circle needs no change; only the second is divided, by 3.
steps.why: The second circle's leading coefficient of 3 must be divided out of every term before it can be subtracted from S, which is already in standard form.
common_mistakes: Dividing the first circle by 3 as well, when it does not need it — only the circle actually printed with a leading coefficient other than 1 needs standardising.
Dividing the −7x and 8y terms by 3 but leaving the constant −11 undivided.
steps.memory_tip: Check each circle's OWN leading coefficient separately — here only one of the two needs the standardising step.

steps.label: Subtract to find the radical axis
steps.margin_note: Second mark, for the subtraction and the cleared final line.
steps.why: Subtracting the two standard-form circles cancels x² and y², leaving the radical axis; multiplying through by −3/2 clears every fraction to give whole-number coefficients.
common_mistakes: Computing −3 − (−7/3) as −3 − 7/3 instead of −3 + 7/3, a sign slip that changes the whole line.
Leaving the equation as −2x − 20y + 26 = 0 instead of dividing through by −2 to reach the simplest form.
steps.memory_tip: −3 = −9/3, so −3 + 7/3 = −2/3 — always convert whole numbers to the same denominator as the fraction before adding.
